subject: PulseWave realtime blocking: sustained chunked-transfer timeouts and SLA risk
messages:
From: Alexandra Cho <alexandra.cho@pulsewave.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PulseWave demo: repeated realtime stalls during ramp — logs attached

Hi Tessa / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. During the 11:00 PDT demo we saw multiple periods where the model simply stopped streaming for ~6-12s before resuming — consumers saw blank tokens and the websocket connection stayed open but produced no chunks. This happened on three sessions and looks correlated with higher concurrent input rates (we're running 12 concurrent sessions in the trial).

I've attached a small sample of the stdout and the session traces from one of the stalled sessions. The team is hitting this in our QA and it is blocking our timeline for production cutover next week. Can you confirm if this is something on our side or on Redwood?

Quick details:
- SDK v1.4.2 (Java) using websocket chunked transfer
- Request pattern: short prompts, long-ish expected outputs (~800 tokens)
- Region: us-west-2

Attached: session-traces-0828.zip (contains connection logs + token timestamps), pulsewave_sample_output_snippets.txt

We appreciate a quick triage.

—Alexandra
Alexandra Cho
SRE Lead, PulseWave
alexandra.cho@pulsewave.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PulseWave demo: repeated realtime stalls during ramp — logs attached

Alexandra — thanks for the detailed reproduction and attachments. I'm escalating this to our realtime team immediately. Initial read: the pattern you described (open WS, long silence, then resume) is consistent with chunk buffering at the proxy layer or intermittent backpressure in the serving tier; we need to verify whether chunks are queued on the server or lost in transit.

Immediate next steps from our side (doing now):
1) SEs will reproduce with your payloads and the same concurrency you reported.
2) We'll enable verbose WS tracing on your trial session IDs and share a filtered trace within 2 hours.
3) If we see server-side queuing, we'll route the trial to an isolated pool (no tenant multiplexing) and test again — this is a quick mitigation we can do without downtime.

Could you confirm the sample session IDs in the zip are from the 11:00 PDT run and share any additional session IDs if available? Also please let me know whether you can tolerate a rolling route change for the trial while we investigate (we expect minimal disruption).

I'll keep you updated. Apologies for the hit to your testing window — we'll prioritize.

Best,

Tessa Morgan

Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: PulseWave — escalate to execs if mitigation not immediate

Team — fyi I'm following this and recommend we prep an executive brief if we cannot deliver the isolated pool mitigation within the next 4 hours. PulseWave is in an active renewal conversation (deal PW-4321) and the customer is explicit about production readiness next week.

Summary for execs (draft):
- Problem: Intermittent streaming stalls (6-12s) under mid-concurrency load, appears as chunked-transfer silence while connection remains established.
- Impact: Blocks customer production cutover; perceived SLA failure; renewal at risk.
- Immediate mitigation: Route customer to isolated serving pool, enable aggressive keepalive & smaller chunk flush interval, gather full traces.
- Escalation ask: If mitigation fails, request C-suite note and offer pro-rated credits + tech-led exec sync.

Tessa — if SEs confirm server-side queuing, I'd like a short one-page timeline and proposed credit figure so we can present to SVP Sales / CFO.

Vanessa
Director, Customer Reliability
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: PulseWave — escalate to execs if mitigation not immediate

Quick technical read from the sample traces (attached original zip). Key findings:
- Timestamps show token emission pauses align with a burst of concurrent requests hitting the same worker host.
- HTTP chunk flushes stop for the silent window; no TCP resets noted.
- Proxy-level metrics show socket write buffer saturation and repeated EAGAIN on several hosts.

Short-term mitigation I executed at 11:20 PDT (results attached):
- Rerouted trial sessions to a dedicated 2-node pool (isolated) and dropped per-chunk buffer size from 32KB to 8KB. Immediate tests show consistent streaming with ~<200ms inter-token intervals.
- Enabled keepalive pinging at 10s and enabled forced flush on our runtime for sessions with expected outputs >500 tokens.

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Patch candidate to handle write backpressure more gracefully landed on staging (PR: SUP-2147). Need quick verification and can promote to prod in ~3 hours pending signoff.
- Recommend we prepare a customer communication (apology + mitigation summary + offer) and brief the Sales execs for renewal sensitivity.

Attachments: filtered-trace-0829.txt (generated), demo-reroute-results-0829.txt

-David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: PulseWave update: mitigation in place and proposed next steps

Alexandra / James — thanks for your patience. Quick update from our triage:

What happened
- Under increased concurrent session load we observed proxy-level write-buffer saturation that caused the runtime to batch chunk emissions and wait for socket availability, which manifested as the streaming silence you saw.

What we did (completed)
- Immediately routed your trial traffic to an isolated pool to remove noisy neighbors (11:20 PDT).
- Reduced internal chunk buffer size and enabled forced flush on long outputs.
- Deployed keepalive pings to prevent intermediate proxies from stalling long-lived connections.

Outcome
- Re-run of your demo traffic pattern shows no 6-12s stalls; token flow steady (<200ms intervals) across 25 repeated runs. We captured traces and attached the demo-reroute-results-0829.txt for your review.

Proposed next steps
1) Allow us to leave your trial on the isolated pool through your cutover next week (minimal performance delta).
2) We will promote a patch to address write backpressure handling (SUP-2147) to prod tonight — target 02:00 PDT with a 30-minute maintenance window.
3) As a gesture for the disruption to your QA window, Vanessa will follow up on a pro-rated service credit; we suggest 10% for the trial week but are open to discussion.
4) Offer: Executive sync with our CTO and your engineering leadership tomorrow at 10:00 PDT to align on long-term reliability commitments.

Please confirm whether the isolated pool is OK and if you accept the exec sync time. Again, apologies — we know timing is sensitive for your cutover.

Best regards,

Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
